questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate follow-up.

cells: P waves 82/min, wide QRS 34/min, PR varies
Metoprolol plus diltiazem started 10 days ago

rationale.correct: Complete heart block with hypotension and altered mental status is unstable bradycardia; the drug combination is the likely cause.

perOption.r1: Atria and ventricles beat independently: third-degree (complete) heart block.
perOption.r2: Hypotension shows the slow rate is not perfusing the client.
perOption.r3: Altered mental status is a sign of poor cerebral perfusion.
perOption.r4: Two AV nodal blockers together can cause high-grade block.
perOption.r5: Normal; hypoglycemia does not explain the drowsiness.
perOption.r6: Normal; there is no sign of infarction.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of unstable bradycardia.

questions.stem: For each finding, choose what it means.

cells.text: Regular P waves and regular QRS complexes with PR intervals that vary

options.text: No atrial impulses are conducted to the ventricles
Every other atrial impulse is conducted
The PR lengthens until a beat is dropped
Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response
The escape rhythm starts below the AV node
The escape rhythm starts in the AV junction
A bundle branch block with sinus rhythm
Additive slowing of conduction through the AV node

rationale.correct: Complete heart block with a wide ventricular escape is unstable and unlikely to respond to atropine; the drug combination is the cause.

perOption.b1:a: This is the defining sign of third-degree block.
perOption.b1:b: That is 2:1 second-degree block, with a fixed PR.
perOption.b1:d: Atrial fibrillation has no regular P waves.
perOption.b2:a: A wide, slow escape rhythm comes from the ventricles and is unreliable.
perOption.b2:b: A junctional escape is narrow and runs at 40 to 60/min.
perOption.b2:c: The P waves are not conducted.
perOption.b3:a: Beta blockers and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers both slow AV conduction.
perOption.b3:b: A potassium of 5.2 adds little; the drugs are the main cause.
perOption.b3:c: This is a predictable drug effect.
perOption.b3:d: The timing points to the new drug.

questions.educationalObjective: Analyze a rhythm strip and its cause.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The priority is to {{b1}}. Atropine is {{b2}} because {{b3}}.

options.text: raise the heart rate to restore perfusion
the block is below the AV node
the blood pressure is too low

rationale.correct: In unstable complete heart block with a wide escape, the priority is to restore the rate, usually with transcutaneous pacing, because atropine rarely works.

perOption.b1:a: Hypotension and altered mental status need a faster rate now.
perOption.b2:a: Atropine acts on the SA and AV nodes.
perOption.b2:b: It may be tried, but it should not delay pacing.
perOption.b3:a: A wide escape rhythm means the block is below the node, where atropine has no effect, so pacing is prepared at once.
perOption.b3:b: Age does not change its action.
perOption.b3:d: Atropine's limitation is the level of the block.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize treatment of unstable complete heart block.

questions.stem: For each prescription, indicate whether it is indicated or contraindicated for the client now.

rows.text: Transcutaneous pacing
Dopamine infusion if pacing does not restore perfusion
Lidocaine 1 mg/kg IV for the wide QRS complexes
Hold metoprolol and diltiazem
Carotid sinus massage
Glucagon IV if beta blocker toxicity is suspected

rationale.correct: Pace, support with a chronotropic drug if needed, and remove the cause. Never suppress a ventricular escape rhythm or add vagal stimulation.

perOption.r1:c1: Pacing restores the rate while the drug effects wear off.
perOption.r1:c2: Pacing restores the rate while the drug effects wear off.
perOption.r2:c1: A chronotropic infusion is the alternative or addition to pacing.
perOption.r2:c2: A chronotropic infusion is the alternative or addition to pacing.
perOption.r3:c1: Lidocaine would suppress the ventricular escape rhythm that is keeping the client alive.
perOption.r3:c2: Lidocaine would suppress the ventricular escape rhythm that is keeping the client alive.
perOption.r5:c1: Vagal stimulation slows the heart further.
perOption.r5:c2: Vagal stimulation slows the heart further.
perOption.r6:c1: Glucagon raises heart rate by a route that bypasses the beta receptor.
perOption.r6:c2: Glucagon raises heart rate by a route that bypasses the beta receptor.

questions.stem: The nurse is starting transcutaneous pacing. Place the steps in the order the nurse should do them.

items.text: Check the femoral pulse to confirm mechanical capture
Place the pacing pads in the anterior-posterior position
Set the pacing rate to 60 to 70/min
Connect the monitoring leads to the pacing defibrillator
Give analgesia or sedation as prescribed
Increase the output (mA) until each spike is followed by a wide QRS

rationale.correct: Pads and leads, then rate, then output to electrical capture, then a pulse check for mechanical capture, then comfort.

perOption.a: Pads go on first so pacing can start quickly.
perOption.b: The pacer needs the ECG to sense and to show capture.
perOption.c: A rate that restores perfusion is chosen before the output.
perOption.e: A pulse matching the paced rate shows the heart is contracting.
perOption.f: Pacing is painful; once it is working, comfort is addressed.

questions.stem: Pacing is set at 70/min and 65 mA. Review the 1000 findings. For each finding, indicate whether it shows effective pacing or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Each pacing spike followed by a wide QRS
Femoral pulse 70/min
Blood pressure 106/62 mm Hg; client alert and oriented
Client grimacing and rating chest wall pain 8 of 10
Three pacing spikes in a row with no QRS after them
Skin under the pads intact

rationale.correct: Capture is confirmed by a QRS after each spike and a matching pulse. Pain and loss of capture need action.

perOption.r2:c1: Mechanical capture: the paced beats are producing pulses.
perOption.r2:c2: Mechanical capture: the paced beats are producing pulses.
perOption.r3:c1: Perfusion and mental status have recovered.
perOption.r3:c2: Perfusion and mental status have recovered.
perOption.r4:c1: Pacing pain needs analgesia and sedation as prescribed.
perOption.r4:c2: Pacing pain needs analgesia and sedation as prescribed.
perOption.r5:c1: Intermittent loss of capture needs the output raised and the pads checked.
perOption.r5:c2: Intermittent loss of capture needs the output raised and the pads checked.

questions.educationalObjective: Evaluate the effectiveness of transcutaneous pacing.

rows.label: Monitor
cells: Paced rhythm 70/min; one run of three spikes with no QRS

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require follow-up.

segments.text: The client had a pacemaker placed yesterday and
took the left arm out of the sling several times
a small, soft swelling without bleeding
spikes at 60/min with only some followed by a QRS

rationale.correct: Arm movement, dizziness, hiccups and spikes without a QRS point to lead displacement with failure to capture.

perOption.s2: Raising or moving the arm on the device side early can pull a new lead out of position.
perOption.s4: Dizziness with a slow rate suggests poor output from failed pacing.
perOption.s6: Persistent hiccups can mean the lead is pacing the diaphragm after moving or perforating.
perOption.s8: A small, stable hematoma is common; it is watched, not urgent.
perOption.s10: Spikes without a QRS are failure to capture.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of pacemaker malfunction.

questions.stem: For each telemetry finding in a client with a pacemaker set at a lower rate of 60/min, indicate what it shows.

rows.text: A pacing spike followed by a wide QRS
A pacing spike with no QRS after it
No spikes while the client's own rhythm is 76/min
A spike falling on the T wave just after the client's own beat
Spikes at 60/min while the client's own rhythm is 40/min

rationale.correct: Capture means a QRS after each spike; sensing means no spike when the client's own rate is above the set rate.

perOption.r2:c1: The impulse fired but did not depolarize the ventricle.
perOption.r2:c2: The impulse fired but did not depolarize the ventricle.
perOption.r2:c3: The impulse fired but did not depolarize the ventricle.

perOption.r3:c2: The pacemaker senses the faster intrinsic rhythm and holds back; this is correct.
perOption.r3:c3: The pacemaker senses the faster intrinsic rhythm and holds back; this is correct.
perOption.r4:c1: The pacemaker did not sense the intrinsic beat and fired anyway, which can trigger ventricular tachycardia.

questions.stem: For each possible cause of the client's failure to capture, indicate how likely it is.

rows.text: The ventricular lead has moved out of position
Raised potassium increasing the capture threshold
Battery depletion of the new generator
A hematoma at the incision

perOption.r1:c1: Early after insertion, arm movement plus hiccups strongly suggest a displaced lead.
perOption.r1:c2: Early after insertion, arm movement plus hiccups strongly suggest a displaced lead.

perOption.r2:c1: Electrolyte changes can raise the threshold; a potassium level is checked.
perOption.r2:c2: Electrolyte changes can raise the threshold; a potassium level is checked.
perOption.r2:c3: Electrolyte changes can raise the threshold; a potassium level is checked.
perOption.r3:c1: A new generator has a full battery.
perOption.r3:c2: A new generator has a full battery.
perOption.r3:c3: A new generator has a full battery.
perOption.r4:c1: A small hematoma does not affect the lead in the heart.
perOption.r4:c2: A small hematoma does not affect the lead in the heart.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize causes of pacemaker failure to capture.

questions.stem: Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: A chest x-ray to check lead position
A 12-lead ECG and a device check by the pacemaker team
Range-of-motion exercises of the left arm above the shoulder
An MRI of the chest to locate the lead
Increase the metoprolol dose for the hiccups

rationale.correct: Confirm the lead position, check the device and electrolytes, and have backup pacing ready.

perOption.a: Shows whether the lead has moved.
perOption.b: Confirms the problem and the thresholds.
perOption.c: Backup if the rate or pressure falls further.
perOption.e: Raising the arm on the device side must wait until the lead heals in, usually 4 to 6 weeks.
perOption.f: MRI is unsafe with a new device unless it is MRI-conditional and programmed.
perOption.g: Beta blockers do not treat hiccups and would slow the rate.

options.text: Do not raise the left arm above the shoulder for about 4 weeks
Keep the incision dry until the provider says it can be soaked

perOption.a: Lets the lead heal into the heart wall.
perOption.b: Prevents infection of the device pocket.
perOption.c: Overhead movement can displace the lead.
perOption.d: Strong magnets in phones can interfere.
perOption.f: MRI can damage or reprogram some devices.
perOption.h: Persistent hiccups may mean the lead has moved.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of ventricular tachycardia with ICD shocks.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The client's VT is currently {{b1}} because {{b2}}. The most likely trigger is {{b3}}.

options.text: the client is alert with a systolic pressure above 90 mm Hg
the troponin is only slightly raised
hypokalemia from the higher furosemide dose

rationale.correct: Stable monomorphic VT with a reversible trigger: correct potassium and magnesium and give an antidysrhythmic.

perOption.b1:a: The client has a pulse, is alert, and has an acceptable blood pressure.
perOption.b1:b: There is no hypotension, altered mentation, ischemic chest pain or acute heart failure.
perOption.b2:a: Stability is judged by perfusion, not by the rate.
perOption.b2:b: Rate alone does not decide stability.
perOption.b2:c: The ICD's function does not define stability.
perOption.b3:a: Low potassium lowers the threshold for VT.
perOption.b3:c: Troponin is only slightly raised and there is no ST elevation reported.

questions.stem: For each complication, indicate whether it is the most immediate threat or a lesser threat now.

rows.text: Degeneration of VT to ventricular fibrillation or pulseless VT
Acute heart failure from the fast rate
Psychological distress from the shocks
Kidney injury from the creatinine of 1.4

perOption.r2:c1: A weak ventricle tolerates VT poorly and can fail quickly.

perOption.r3:c1: Real and important, but after rhythm control.
perOption.r3:c2: Real and important, but after rhythm control.
perOption.r4:c1: A mild rise that is monitored.
perOption.r4:c2: A mild rise that is monitored.

Synchronized cardioversion

questions.stem: At 1925 the client becomes unresponsive. The monitor shows VT, the ICD has not fired, and there is no carotid pulse. Place the nurse's actions in order.

items.text: Start compressions at once and continue for 2 minutes
Call for help and the code team
Give epinephrine 1 mg IV after the second shock
Deliver an unsynchronized shock through the pads
Check the rhythm and shock again if VT persists

rationale.correct: In a monitored pulseless VT with pads on: call for help, shock, compress for 2 minutes, recheck and shock again, then epinephrine.

perOption.a: Help is summoned at once; the pads are already on.
perOption.b: In a monitored arrest with pads on, defibrillation comes first.
perOption.c: Compressions follow the shock without a pulse check.
perOption.d: The rhythm is checked after 2 minutes of CPR.
perOption.e: Epinephrine follows the second shock in shockable rhythms.

questions.stem: After one shock, the client has a pulse and is on an amiodarone infusion. Review the 2300 findings. For each finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Sinus rhythm 74/min with no further VT
Potassium 4.2 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL
QTc 528 ms (442 ms on admission)
Blood pressure 84/50 mm Hg during the infusion
Alert, oriented, follows commands
Peripheral IV site red and painful along the vein

perOption.r5:c1: Neurologic recovery after a brief arrest.
perOption.r5:c2: Neurologic recovery after a brief arrest.
perOption.r6:c1: Amiodarone irritates veins; the site needs changing, ideally to a central line.

questions.stem: Highlight the values that show the heart is failing as a pump.

rationale.correct: Low cardiac index with high wedge pressure, plus signs of poor tissue perfusion, define cardiogenic shock.

perOption.r1: A cardiac index below 2.2 shows severely reduced output.
perOption.r2: High left-sided filling pressure: the left ventricle cannot empty.
perOption.r3: Tissues are using anaerobic metabolism because of poor perfusion.
perOption.r5: Compensatory; it follows from low output rather than showing pump failure itself.
perOption.r6: High SVR is the body's compensation by vasoconstriction, not pump failure itself.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize hemodynamic cues of pump failure.

questions.stem: For each hemodynamic pattern, choose the type of shock it fits.

rationale.correct: Wedge pressure, cardiac index and SVR together separate cardiogenic, hypovolemic and distributive shock.

perOption.b1:a: The pump fails, so pressure backs up and the vessels constrict.
perOption.b1:d: Neurogenic shock has low SVR and bradycardia.
perOption.b2:a: Low volume lowers filling pressure and output, with compensatory vasoconstriction.
perOption.b2:b: Wedge pressure is high in cardiogenic shock.
perOption.b3:a: Vasodilation lowers SVR, and output rises to compensate.
perOption.b3:b: Output is low in cardiogenic shock.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The client is in {{b1}} shock caused by {{b2}}, and the treatment goal is to {{b3}}.

options.text: improve contractility and perfusion without adding volume
give fluid until the wedge pressure rises
lower the heart rate with a beta blocker

rationale.correct: Cardiogenic shock after anterior MI needs contractility support and perfusion, not more volume.

perOption.b1:a: Pump failure after a large anterior MI.
perOption.b2:a: An anterior MI can destroy enough muscle to cause pump failure.
perOption.b3:a: The heart is full but weak; it needs an inotrope and perfusion support, not fluid.
perOption.b3:c: A negative inotrope would worsen shock.
perOption.b3:d: A higher afterload makes the failing ventricle work harder.

Mechanical circulatory support, such as an intra-aortic balloon pump
Metoprolol 5 mg IV for the tachycardia
Nitroprusside infusion to lower the afterload

rationale.correct: Support contractility and pressure, add mechanical support if needed, and avoid fluid, negative inotropes and vasodilators while the client is hypotensive.

questions.stem: Dobutamine is prescribed at 5 mcg/kg/minute. The premixed bag contains dobutamine 500 mg in 250 mL. The client weighs 90 kg. At what rate should the nurse set the pump? Record your answer to one decimal place.

rationale.correct: 5 mcg/kg/min x 90 kg = 450 mcg/min. 450 x 60 = 27,000 mcg/hour = 27 mg/hour. The bag is 500 mg/250 mL = 2 mg/mL, so 27 / 2 = 13.5 mL/hour.

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 0930
exhibits.body: A 79-year-old client fainted at home this morning. The client has hypertension and atrial flutter that converted last year. Medications: metoprolol tartrate 50 mg twice daily; diltiazem ER 240 mg daily, added by a different provider 10 days ago; lisinopril 10 mg daily. The client is drowsy and answers slowly, and the skin is cool and pale. Monitor: P waves regular at 82/min; QRS complexes wide (0.14 s) and regular at 34/min; PR intervals vary with no pattern.

The incision has a small, soft swelling with no active bleeding.
